column1: # Divergence-visibility fixtures.  Consumed by capture.sh and check.sh.
# name    the <name>.spthy in this directory.  A row named <fixture>@<variant>
#         loads <fixture>.spthy under another set of flags; its captures are
#         named after the whole row name.  A fixture may bring sibling files
#         it reads itself: an `#include`d <fixture>.inc, an oracle script
# slice   comma-separated list of blocks cut from ONE theory load:
#           wf      the wellformedness report block (wf_gate.sh's slice)
#           summary the run summary, which carries the wellformedness count
#           stdout  the whole stdout (`--parse-only` and `-m` documents,
#                   fatal reports printed before the exit)
#           error   exit code and normalized error kind for a fatal run
#           error-message  exit code and full diagnostic for a fatal run
#           traces  the --output-dot and --output-json files, which the
#                   scripts add to the row's flags
# mode    match    the port must reproduce the captured oracle bytes
#         diverge  the port must reproduce <name>.<slice>.rs.txt, which must
#                  still differ from the captured oracle bytes.  mode is per
#                  ROW, so every slice a `diverge` row lists has to diverge on
#                  its own — a slice the two engines agree on reads as the
# flags   extra prover flags, passed to BOTH engines
# input   optional theory path relative to this directory, overriding <fixture>.spthy
# Local fixture headers explain the regression. For an upstream input, the
# comment on its row explains which invocation exercises it.
# The pinned 5G model reaches the forbidden-chain regression with this heuristic.
